title: Spheres on Spheres
caption: An Auxiliary Telescope, the Moon and Venus lined up, Paranal Observatory
celestial: Landscape photograph; the source does not name the site

recognition.text: ESO Picture of the Week (an editorial selection, not an audience score).

story: Three very different spheres line up at ESO's Very Large Telescope at Paranal Observatory in Chile. The largest, in the foreground, is one of the telescope's four Auxiliary Telescopes. Above it floats the Moon, and near the top of the frame is Venus.

The setting Sun lights only a thin sliver of the Moon. Even so, some of the lunar maria can be seen. These are the dark, sea-like areas left by lava flows early in the Moon's history. Venus is the second planet from the Sun and one of Earth's planetary neighbours.

The Auxiliary Telescopes are movable, and they can be arranged in different configurations to suit different scientific goals. From where the photographer stood, this one lined up with the Moon and Venus above it. Astrophotographer and ESO Photo Ambassador Yuri Beletsky caught the alignment during one of his visits to the observatory.

understand.summary: A ground-based photograph by Yuri Beletsky for ESO, taken in visible light. The colours are those the camera recorded.
understand.eye: The Moon and Venus are both visible to the unaided eye, and it is the camera's viewpoint that lines them up with the telescope.

behind.exposure: Not published on the source page.

explore: The photograph is titled Spheres on Spheres. Beletsky was fortunate to catch the three objects lined up in the sky.
alt: A spherical telescope enclosure in the foreground with a thin sliver of Moon floating above it and Venus near the top of the sky.
